User-facing agentteams init/start/status/work/stop facade; init delegates v3 bootstrap to initializeLocalConfig and lifecycle delegates to the compiled runtime local launcher. It owns no TLS, child projection, capability implementation or network truth. Candidate evidence: c3c2e0e; U2 continuation: docs/evidence/776fcad-u2-config-impl-20261003/. The ACP `--serve <opencode|dsh> --ip --port` entry is delivered here: cli/agentteams.mjs parses the flags and dispatches to runtime/acp-serve.ts, which starts one daemon plus one engine child with the OpenCode or DSH adapter selected by runtime/acp-serve.ts engineAdapterFor. No compile-only placeholder exists. D04 adds the `agentteams registry start|status|stop --config <file> [--generation <n>]` verbs; they delegate lifecycle truth to runtime/registry-process.ts and start no other daemon.

Owns the source-level local Work Unix socket seam only: typed decode/encode, listener admission, peer drain and own-socket cleanup, plus the single failed or unconfirmed Work receipt projection from a typed frame. It is not the CLI facade, receiver dispatch, config internal owner, or installed runtime.
Owns the single staged package producer, base asset/CLI smoke, installed lifecycle restart smoke, and lifecycle receipt binding. Final SDK runner/graph inclusion remains a D3/U4 input dependency.

Owns link configuration, transport, health and route execution. D04 adds `network/registration-client.ts` as the client transport/health owner for registry registration: it connects the config-selected discovery endpoint over wss, registers, renews the presence lease with a heartbeat, reconnects with bounded backoff on the same endpoint and keeps the original error instead of switching servers. It imports no `config/**`; the config-selected discovery plan and the AgentDeclaration stay in runtime. Gate: teams-acp-d04-registry. D05 adds the connection layer: `network/teams-negotiation.ts` (the frozen-frame negotiation state machine and the only source of an agreement), `network/teams-session.ts` (one authenticated connection bridged to the injected AcpHost, with locally allocated refs and generation/engine rewrite at the receive boundary), `network/teams-connection-history.ts` (typed kind=connection history over the injected store) and `network/teams-membership.ts` (the per-remote-agent connection/role view assembled from the directory, route and registration surfaces). D05 also adds the additive `RegistrationClient.publish` surface that carries the daemon's real listener route plus its ACP capability over the same D04 path. Gate: teams-acp-d05-network. The D05 closure adds two modules to this owner: `network/teams-ingress.ts` owns the one inbound Teams connection lifecycle on an already authenticated direct-WSS connection, runs the responder negotiation, allocates this side's own transport-scoped connectionId/channelId before any host call so the peer wire ref never reaches the AcpHost, creates the Teams session, and records the typed connection.negotiated / channel.opened / channel.closed / connection.failed facts; `network/teams-status.ts` owns the read-only `TeamsStatusPort` that projects the live connection ledger through projectTeamsMembership and reads the durable connection history, which is the D06 read handoff and stores no state of its own. Gate: teams-acp-d05-network, which now also runs network/teams-ingress.spec.ts, network/teams-status.spec.ts and control-protocol/teams-connection.spec.ts. L9 adds `network/teams-egress.ts` to this owner: it is the outbound initiator counterpart of `network/teams-ingress.ts` on an already authenticated direct-WSS connection. It runs the initiator negotiation, records connection.negotiated / connection.failed, observes channel lifecycle with local refs only, and opens the one ACP channel through createTeamsSession.open() so the handshake, the inbound mapping, the delivery pump and the release rules keep their single owner. It reuses createTeamsFrameTransport and TeamsConnectionLedger from the ingress owner, declares no second envelope and never sends acp.open_ack. Gate: teams-acp-d05-network, which now also runs network/teams-egress.spec.ts. L9 command-side adds this module's one production caller in the runtime owner (`runtime/serve-egress.ts`), so the network module itself is unchanged and declares no dial path of its own.

Canonical owner of the Console observation wire contract. BB09 round 12 adds the optional capabilityDetails declaration summary to the shared runtime|directory Agent row fields, its closed parser validation (existing string and capacity/unit checks; illegal shapes rejected, never stripped) and the single declaration-to-summary helper reused by the runtime and Console-hub producers. D00 adds the public ACP envelope and single fault carrier (acp.ts), the type-only engine adapter port (engine.ts), the Teams negotiation frames and the connection-state/history DTOs (teams-connection.ts, teams-state.ts); declarations and parsers only; when this note was written transport, negotiation and history reads were pending D01/D05/D06. 2026-10-14 correction: D01, D05 and D06 now implement those in their own modules, so this module still owns declarations and parsers only.

Owns Session, RPC/callback correlation, execution admission and execution history semantics. D01 (merged 7d0bca4, fixed 75a6cf4) implements `agent-host/acp-host.ts` and the append-only write port `agent-host/acp-history.ts`: per-channel id correlation, explicit Session ownership, D00 policy before any engine write, append-before-effect with separate history-fault reporting, cancel.requested versus the prompt's terminal result, RESULT_UNKNOWN on engine exit or channel close, and bounded delivery/notification records. Status is partial, not implemented: the host is exercised through the real CLI process by the committed D02 and D03 black boxes, with both engine adapters wired through the one `--serve` entry, and, since the D05 closure, the D05 network channel is wired into this host: runtime/acp-serve.ts buildLanChannel routes its authenticated LAN ingress into openTeamsIngress, which hands the host a real locally allocated AcpChannelRef. 2026-10-14 correction: the earlier text here said the D05 network channel is not wired and that the host has no live product evidence; the channel is wired and live --serve black boxes exercise this host (docs/evidence/acp-d02-integration-20261010, acp-d03-serve-20261010), while installed-copy and published-release evidence for this module still does not exist.D06 PART 2 owns the permission option decision path on this boundary: projectPermissionOptions projects the engine-supplied session/request_permission options verbatim into the frozen ConsolePermissionOption set (absent when the engine offered none, and a malformed or ambiguous set refused with INVALID_ACP_FRAME before delivery), while adjudicatePermissionReply answers the engine only with an optionId it really offered. A selection the engine never offered, a selection when no options were offered, an unknown outcome or a missing or stale callback is refused typed and never becomes an approval. Gate: teams-acp-d06-control. 2026-10-14 session-write-side: this owner now also exposes the two read facts a Session write needs, AcpHost.pendingPermissions() and AcpHost.channelForSession(), because it is the A2.6 permission owner and the only place that knows which Session each open channel owns. The permission identity a Console write names is the callback id the controller received, which is also the reply address; the host keeps its own history record id as the durable audit identity. A2.6 is not weakened: the reader refuses a stale, absent or ambiguous callback and never invents an optionId. Gate: teams-acp-l9-session-write-side.

Owns the optional, non-permanent Console observation/configuration transport: the authenticated HTTP/SSE surface, the frozen Console API dispatch, and the static UI/API server. Delivered as `console-host/` (`@deepseek-ai/teams-console-host`): `src/auth.ts` (exact-credential Basic auth plus the cross-site guard), `src/server.ts` (static root, extension allowlist and realpath containment for `/ui/`), `src/http-api.ts` (typed refusals, SSE snapshots, close on owner loss) and `src/console-api.ts`. `runtime/control-process.ts:15-16` imports `createConsoleAuthorization`/`createConsoleServer` from it, so D06 and D07 run on this module. Status is partial, not implemented: there is no published-release evidence, and no installed-copy evidence for the console host outside a control daemon. 2026-10-14 correction (L11): the installed console host now serves the frozen console to a real browser from an installed npm package — docs/evidence/acp-l11-installed-browser-20261014/ (18 checks, exit 0) shows the document and all 18 /ui/ modules byte-identical to the installed package's files, rendered by real Chrome. The D08 acceptance run also exercises it through the installed tarball's control entrypoint. This entry previously read `status: design` with no note, which contradicted both the delivered code and `function-map.json`, where `independent_console_http_server` and `console_v1_http_transport` already name `master-host` as owner. Corrected here; the ownership itself was already right and is unchanged. Gate: teams-acp-d06-control.

Owner of the engine-independent stdio ACP transport between an engine child and agent-host. D01 (merged 7d0bca4, fixed 75a6cf4) implements `acp-adapter/stdio.ts` as the newline-delimited JSON `AcpDuplex` over the frozen `control-protocol/engine.ts` port, with CRLF tolerance, a maxFrameBytes bound, typed transport faults and clean-EOF settlement; `acp-adapter/test-peer.mjs` is a labeled test peer, not an engine. The directory exists now. Status is partial, not implemented: the D03 DSH adapter and the D02 OpenCode adapter each compile a real `EngineLaunchSpec` (see the dsh-adapter and opencode-adapter modules), and runtime/acp-serve.ts dispatches both engine kinds over this one transport; installed-copy engine inference is still not proven here. Gate: teams-acp-d01-host.

Owner of the DSH engine adapter: it derives the real DSH native profile patch from the accepted Teams config, compiles the single `EngineLaunchSpec` for the `dsh` kind, and reads the real `initialize`/`session/new` results back as an effectiveness proof. D03 (frozen candidate 60bf76b, merged here) implements `dsh-adapter/index.ts` and `dsh-adapter/native-config.ts` with 31 focused specs, and `dsh-adapter/real-engine-evidence.mjs` is committed evidence tooling that drove the real installed DSH 0.2.0-rc.2 through the real D01 runtime for 18/18 gates. It reuses the frozen `control-protocol/engine.ts` port, the D00 config/policy owners and the D01 runtime; it adds no second Session path, stdio transport or config source. The `--serve dsh` wiring delivered by this candidate composes it through `runtime/acp-serve.ts` `engineAdapterFor` with the same daemon/host/stdio/readiness/stop code as `--serve opencode`, and the entry removes the owned DSH home on stop and on a failed start. It also declares its own `enforceablePolicies`, derived from `dshHasPolicyEnforcementOwner` over its declared surface, so the blacklist classes the D01 host really enforces (including `capability:` and `client-capability:` keys) are accepted while a key with no enforcement owner is still refused, and the runtime never substitutes `declaredMethods`. Status stays partial, not implemented: the DSH black-box evidence is a live local run against one provider route rather than an installed-copy receipt, the AppSDK compile/verify gate is blocked by the pre-existing 0.1.0014 pin mismatch, and `resource_link` prompts stay refused while the real DSH initialize advertises `embeddedContext: false`. Gate: teams-acp-d03-dsh.

Owns config intent, provider/catalog/model and policy compilation. D00 adds the v4 single-daemon intent compiler and CLI override/effective readback (config/daemon-intent.ts) plus the ACP capability vocabulary (config/acp-policy.ts). The compiler is a library contract; when this note was written no CLI or runtime caller started a daemon from it. 2026-10-14 correction: the --serve entry (cli/agentteams.mjs -> runtime/acp-serve.ts) and the control and registry verbs now compile one daemon intent and start that daemon. 2026-10-14 intent-side: config/relations-intent-store.ts owns the durable desired-relations record (one CAS write path, atomic rename, typed malformed/conflict/uncertain results) as the one CAS store. The control daemon is its single writer and the agent daemon its single reader: the record path is the shared derivation <home>/.agentteams/relations/<accountId>/<scopeId>/relations-intent.json, so both sides resolve it from their own accepted facts without a new config key. 2026-10-14 session-write-side: config/session-intent-store.ts owns the sibling durable pending-Session-write record and its reader watermark, one record per target agent at <home>/.agentteams/sessions/<accountId>/<scopeId>/<agentId>/session-intent.json, so the frozen Session write commands keep one owner and no second store. 2026-10-15 session-projection: config/session-observation-store.ts owns the sibling durable Session-observation record, one record per agent in the same directory layout, carrying only projection rows (the Session ids an open channel really owns and each pending permission callback with its controller-visible id) and never a transcript, a permission option set or a credential; config/durable-record.ts holds the one atomic write discipline (mode-0o600 temp plus rename, with the failed/uncertain/applied outcomes) that the intent store, its watermark, the observation store and config/relations-intent-store.ts all use, so the duplicated durable-write helpers F4 recorded are gone: the relations store's own persist/uncertainty/discard were deleted in this change and its gate teams-acp-l9-intent-side then measured 72 passed / 4 files, exit 0 (committed log gate-l9-intent-side-4files.log).

Owns Relay link admission/lifetime and closeGrant revocation. 4e04166 is bound to docs/design/teams-relay-link-lifetime.md and docs/design/dagpipe/graphs/relay-link.graph.json under required teams-relay-link-topology. Static governance bindings are not Work SDK Operators. The opened pair continues after the admission deadline while original controls/generations stay current; server/relay.spec.ts covers the public TLS/WSS behavior. D04 adds the server-owned presence lease in server/relay.ts (DEFAULT_PEER_TTL_MS 90s, one unref'd sweep timer, offline publication that keeps the entry/declaration/generation as history) and server/registry-intent.ts as the single mapping site from the frozen RegistryDaemonIntent to RelayServerOptions, including the explicit TLS_REQUIRED refusal and credential loading. Gate: teams-acp-d04-registry. Public deployment remains deferred.

Work DAGpipe SDK host adapter and runner are implemented as a source-level library consumer (runtime/dagpipe/** with real compiled SDK and provider-ledger tests), and AgentWorkClient capability selection is implemented. The launcher local Work ingress is delivered for the exact candidate: the public CLI/launcher/receiver path and the installed runtime consumer are covered by the installed package user smoke, which drives installed submit/query plus persistent open/request/query/close against installed runtime artifacts. runtime/acp-serve.ts owns the user --serve entry for both engine kinds: it reads one v4 agent intent, refuses an unbound agent or a non-loopback listener that declares no [discovery] server with a typed fault, dispatches through engineAdapterFor to the OpenCode or DSH adapter, starts exactly one daemon plus one engine child over the D01 runtime, serves the local channel and, when classifyServeListener reports the lan class, the authenticated direct-WSS LAN channel, reports readiness only from the engine's own session/new response and stops by explicit signal, removing the owned engine home. Provider ledger and admission remain Agent-owned; no second daemon or scheduler. D04 adds runtime/registry-process.ts (the registry daemon lifecycle: one detached child, PID + startToken + generation ownership in the daemon dataDirectory, readiness published by the child itself, and a stop that kills only the matched pid) and runtime/registry-registration.ts (the config-selected discovery plan, credential/CA bootstrap, AgentDeclaration derivation and the standalone registration entry). Gate: teams-acp-d04-registry. D05 adds the pure `listenerRouteCandidates` and `declarationWithPublishedSurfaces` helpers to runtime/registry-registration.ts: a daemon publishes its real declared listener route plus its ACP capability over the same registration client, with the declaration revision advancing once and identity/scope preserved. No second registry, directory or publication path is added. The D05 closure composes these modules into the user entry: runtime/acp-serve.ts classifies the listener address (classifyServeListener), serves the loopback plain newline-JSON channel on listen.ip or 127.0.0.1:0 for a LAN listener, serves the authenticated direct-WSS LAN channel whose every accepted connection goes through openTeamsIngress, projects the accepted policy into the single acp capability (acpCapabilityDeclarations), and publishes the real listener route plus that capability through the existing D04 path only after the listener is bound and the client is online, with the published revision equal to the LAN target capabilitiesRevision. The stop order is egress rows, LAN listener, local server, registration client, daemon, then the owned engine home. L9 command-side adds `runtime/serve-egress.ts` as the daemon's own egress owner: startAcpServe composes it after the listener and registration are ready and dials every peer the accepted intent declares, reading the responder's published capability revision through the existing D04 directory snapshot and the responder's published listener generation from the entry's own constant, refusing a peer with no explicit endpoint typed and recording a typed failure instead of crashing or skipping; the live rows and failures are exposed on the handle, disconnect(agentId) tears one peer down, and stop closes them before the host. Console-offline Work and final user acceptance remain pending; the DSH branch still has no installed-copy replay.The 2026-10-14 intent-side increment closes the control-to-agent loop without a new channel: runtime/control-process.ts is the single writer of the desired-relations record through config/relations-intent-store.ts, and runtime/acp-serve.ts createRelationsIntentWatch polls that record on a named 500ms interval and reconciles the live egress rows (dial a newly desired declared peer, disconnect a live peer the record no longer desires, never dial an undeclared agentId, no-op on a missing record, keep live rows on a broken one), stopping the watch before the egress in stop(). Real entry evidence: docs/evidence/acp-l9-intent-side-20261014/black-box-intent-side.mjs. D06 adds runtime/control-process.ts, the single writer for the control-kind daemon: one detached child with its own durable state record, one WebUI listener, explicit-PID stop, and typed INVALID_CONFIG / UNSUPPORTED_CONFIGURATION / ALREADY_RUNNING / START_TIMEOUT / STOP_TIMEOUT / STALE_GENERATION / STALE_OWNER / INVALID_STATUS / PORT_OCCUPIED / CREDENTIAL_UNAVAILABLE / HISTORY_UNAVAILABLE / STREAM_UNAVAILABLE / UNSUPPORTED_OPERATION failures. The child never starts an engine child, a registry, an implicit master or a second daemon. D06 PART 2 binds the real D05 network status port at its single injection point: createControlNetworkStatus composes createTeamsConnectionLedger, createTeamsConnectionHistory over the daemon own createAcpHistoryStore, the D04 registration client and projectTeamsMembership, then returns the D05 owner createTeamsStatusPort; the daemon keeps the structurally unbound path as a typed absence, projects the honest empty connections list when no channel is established, kept the frozen read port read-only (before the 2026-10-14 intent-side increment it refused a connection mutation typed because that port declares no mutation; since then the three A2.4 relation commands are routed to the durable desired-relations write instead of a typed refusal), and never infers online or execution state from history. Gate: teams-acp-d06-control. 2026-10-14 intent-side: runtime/control-process.ts writes that record from the three frozen relation commands, and runtime/acp-serve.ts adds createRelationsIntentWatch so the agent daemon reconciles its own egress rows against it on a named interval. 2026-10-15 session-projection: runtime/session-observation-publisher.ts publishes the Sessions and pending permissions the daemon's own AcpHost really holds, and runtime/acp-serve.ts runs it on the same named interval plus once in its own stop(), so a stopped agent's rows disappear without a timeout heuristic. runtime/control-process.ts adds readObservedSessionProjection so the control daemon's real Console projection carries those rows under the agent that owns them, and AcpHost gains the read-only openedSessions() that reports the Session ids an open channel holds. The control daemon declares no Teams listener, so no control-to-agent channel is added and the Console is never a data path.

The OpenCode engine adapter (D02, merged candidate 1d4df3a, fixed 1af8fe5/9436aae) is the single compiler of an OpenCode EngineLaunchSpec: compileLaunch derives the managed OpenCode config and its credential env refs from the accepted config, verifyEffective reports the model the engine itself returned from session/new, and declaredMethods/enforceablePolicies declare the adapter capability. runtime/acp-serve.ts is its only production caller. Gate teams-acp-d02-opencode stays partial because the real-engine command needs an installed opencode plus a local stub provider and is not installed-copy evidence.
